title: One-Pan Red Pepper and Ricotta Rotini
description: Impastable rotini cooks directly in a silky roasted pepper sauce, with ricotta folded through the spirals at the end.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender and tall jug

ingredients.name: peeled roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.note: Use plain home-roasted pepper without brine, with skin and seeds removed.

steps.title: Blend the sauce base
steps.text: Blend {pepper}, {broth} and {garlic} until completely smooth, about 30 seconds.

steps.title: Start the pasta
steps.text: Bring the pepper sauce to a simmer in the HexClad skillet and stir in {rotini}.

steps.title: Cook in the sauce
steps.text: Cover and simmer gently for 10–18 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes to keep the spirals submerged. Check a spiral at 10 minutes and continue until tender throughout, adding hot water a splash at a time if needed.

steps.title: Smooth the ricotta
steps.text: In a cup, whisk {ricotta} with a spoonful of the hot cooking sauce until smooth.

steps.title: Finish the spirals
steps.text: Take the skillet off the heat and fold the loosened ricotta and {basil} through the pasta until the sauce fills the spirals.

notes: Make ahead: Blend the pepper base up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Add the dry pasta only when ready to cook. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The fiber-rich spirals soften with freezing and the ricotta can weep. Fridge reheat: Warm covered in the skillet with a splash of water over medium-low heat for 4–7 minutes, stirring gently until the center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge reheat instructions. Option A uses sweet roasted pepper. For a gentler Option B, use an equal weight of cooked butternut squash. For dairy-free sauce, use smooth unsalted white bean puree in place of ricotta. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 88 kcal, 7.0 g protein, 26.8 g total carbohydrate, 2.8 g fat, 18.6 g fiber, 160 mg sodium.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
